price.quote: The Mod Bikes Black 3 retails for $3,499 but is is sometimes on sale for around $2,699. While it’s on the higher end, the included features like leather ergonomic handles, adjustable suspension, and proprietary easy snap-on accessory system make it a worthy investment for riders who plan on pushing their bike beyond city streets.

wh.quote: Battery | Samsung Li-ion 48V 15Ah (720Wh) - Tested by SGS compliant to UL 2271

The bike uses a Samsung Powerpack Li-ion 48V 15Ah (720Wh) removable battery which is integrated into the bottom half of its frame. Understandably, this is the thickest part of the bike, but I would have liked to see the battery fit in more seamlessly — it has a bit of a lip sticking out that interrupts the otherwise sleek design.

notes: Two maker pages: the main MOD Black 3 (ships Class 2, adjustable to 1 or 3, 20 mph default / 28 mph off-road mode, optional throttle) and a separate 'MOD Black 3 (Class 1)' HSA/FSA version (no throttle, 20 mph, same 750W/69Nm/720Wh, same $2,399 regular). Spec tables are in collapsed accordions; I expanded them to read. Min rider height differs between the two pages (5'6" vs 5'3"). Payload: maker 275 lb vs BikeRide 265 lb (BikeRide says MOD's manual and product page conflict). EBR's MOD Black review is the 2019 Shengyi mid-drive model, not used. Tom's Guide's $3,499 is the old launch price.
